label: Resend
terms_note: Automation is the product: HTTPS-only base https://api.resend.com, Authorization: Bearer re_… (team API key), a User-Agent header is mandatory (403 / error 1010 without it); rate limit 10 requests per second per team across all keys (raisable for approved senders); 429 on excess. Idempotency keys ensure single delivery. Broadcasts / audiences / topics carry Resend's own unsubscribe handling; domains must be verified (DKIM / SPF, optional DMARC / BIMI / custom return path). Receiving: MX records on a verified domain or an auto-managed <id>.resend.app subdomain.

sdks: Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Elixir, Java SDKs; Resend CLI; SMTP relay (https://resend.com/docs/llms.txt)

official_mcp: Resend MCP server (listed in the official docs index for the Receiving API — https://resend.com/docs/llms.txt)

reference.limits: - **10 requests per second per team** across all API keys (raisable for approved senders) → HTTP 429. - Batch ≤ 100 emails; `to` ≤ 50; attachments ≤ 40 MB encoded (client docstring, 2026-09-02 read). - Automation is the intended use; content policy + verified domains; receiving needs MX records.

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: Resend team API key (re_…), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer re_xxxxxxxxx' (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/introduction).

config_fields.name: sender
config_fields.help: Verified-domain sender address used as `from` on every send ('Sender email address', 'Name <email@domain>' allowed; https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email). Env: PLATFORM_MCP_RESEND_SENDER.

adapter.rate_note: '10 requests per second per team' across all API keys → HTTP 429 (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/introduction). 'All API requests must include a User-Agent header' (403 without) — the runtime always sends one.

me.note: Verified by listing one API key (Resend has no account endpoint); account carries the list envelope (object, has_more, data).

send.note: `from` comes from the per-install `sender` config field; `to` is one recipient address; `subject` is required by Resend (the API rejects a missing subject → isError); `text` is sent as the plain-text body; `channel` is ignored. message_id is the Resend email id.

list_inbound.note: Emails received by the team (needs MX on a verified domain). Resend pages by id cursor (`after` / `before`), so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` emails are returned; `since` and `channel` are not sent. The list carries no body: `text` is unset (subject is under raw.subject; the body is on GET /emails/receiving/{id}). `to` is the first recipient.

not_offered.reply: Threading on POST /emails goes through a nested `headers` object (In-Reply-To / References), which the adapter's flat body map cannot express (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email).
not_offered.get_thread: GET /emails/receiving/{id} returns one received email, not a conversation; no thread listing is documented (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/retrieve-received-email).
not_offered.mark_read: No read-state endpoint exists in the Resend API (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/introduction).
